Rick & Morty: Season 9 (2026)

#tvshow

#favorites

watched 8/?/26

rating ★★★★☆

Is it bad to say this is one of my favorite shows ever...I was always a bit embarrassed to ever talk about this show because I felt like the majority of the people in this community was comprised of unironic erm actchually incel redditor discord mods LMAO... but if that is who I must embody to talk about how good this show is then so be it brother... I've always tuned in every time they've released a season and I think this one is one of my favorites! First of all the animation is fucking crazy??? I think they've consistently improved every season when it came to the art direction, but they really blew it out of the park this time. I felt like I was watching a shounen at times because of how fluid some scenes were, so it was a nice surprise to see!! Also I really love the background art (NO ONE EVER TALKS ABOUT IT EITHER..), so colorful and weird which is fitting for a show that explores interdimensional travel. What made this season stand out more than the others prior to it though was how much more positive it felt? This show has always expressed heavy nihilistic themes, but instead of only focusing on the negatives, they had a much more optimistic outlook towards the end of each episode (for the most part) which I think emphasizes these points when you embrace both sides of the whole "nothing matters" rhetoric. I think it also helped that the show remembered to include the development these characters have had over the years. It made all their interactions with one another impactful which was a much better decision than turning them into one-note caricatures. (almost happened to my good friend Jerry Smith) Overall, solid ass season, I feel like you could just watch it without having any knowledge on the lore and have a good time, but it is so much better when you do know too !!!

Companion (2025)

#movie

watched 8/4/26

rating ★★☆☆☆

Was having a hard time trying to decipher whether this movie wanted to be taken seriously or not. On one hand, it attempts to tackle heavier topics, but never really tries to explore any real conflict that could've potentially elevated the storytelling towards saying something more meaningful. Part of the reason I felt this way is because of how many snarky jokes were included throughout the movie? I would've been fine with it if they leaned more into that, but they kind of just sprinkle it in almost as if to deescalate the more serious scenes, so the overall tone ended up falling flat for me personally. I just wish they had committed to one or the other because it stands right in the middle of trying to be a silly, fun comedy sketch and a tense, horrific thriller. Makes me sad because it had such a unique concept too. :-( Also a bit of a personal nitpick but I really wanted to see more of the exoskeleton of the main robot girl...would've been raw as fuck especially when she starts mirking the shit outta everyone!! but they only show a sliver of her hand...lame..........

Obsession (2025)

#movie

watched 6/4/26

rating ★★★☆☆

I think I ranked this 2 stars on my Letterboxd and I feel kinda bad because this movie is more of like a 3 for me. I was just being a hater LMAOO I think my rating wasn't towards the movie specifically, but was more of a sinking realization that a lot of media nowadays that are able to gain mainstream success feel like they are shot to be one big, popular 60-second Youtube short. Idk if this makes any sense, but I guess what I'm trying to say is that every single scene felt as if it was self-contained in that moment rather than extending it's purpose towards moving the story and it's characters. In this movie especially is it guilty of this because once Nikki is possessed does every single scene up the ante all the way to 100...and then it just kinda stays there for the remainder of the movie? While I think it works in those first 10 minutes, does it start to wear down its novelty once every sequence for the next hour and a half is just her regurgitating the same idea, just in slightly different scenarios. Like ok I get that she's possessed and she has no control over her own body and the guy at the scene of the crime is a huge loser idiot coward. But that's as far as it's willing to go and I just wish it delved into the internal struggles that Nikki faces or even explore the sick gratification Bear gains when this all goes down. They only show this ONCE and it was arguably the most memorable part of the movie for me, so I was kind of was hoping it would touch on that area more considering that this movie is almost 2 hours long???? Instead, the film seems to be more interested in displaying the top 10 crazzzyyyy fucked up jumpscares which took away from any development this story could've had and just cheapened the entire message of the movie. I don't know, maybe they all are supposed to be this one-note to get the point across, but if that was all this movie was going to say then it would've worked way better as a short film. Also a bit of a nitpick because I know the budget for this was low, but my god bro I could not see what was going on half of the time because of how dimly lit everything was so it kind of took away from the "scary" moments. Still was mildly entertained and am also ready for everyone to stone me for this take
